observation: Builder src/render/opticCellPresentation.js. Stone deliberately keeps the ordinary displaced common-rock body: opticCellGeometry returns null for stone (122-126), so visualFactory.js:2647-2649 falls through to astDisplacedGeometry('ast_common_rock', def, variantIdx), the same shared cache key ast:geology-v5:ast_common_rock:0 used by ordinary rocks (visualFactory.js:2259-2261). Variant 0 therefore reuses the shared common-rock displacement buffer; nothing stone-specific is allocated. Its material is the cached 'optic:body:stone:v0' MeshStandardMaterial built by buildOpticStoneMaterial(0) (132-160, 248-256), keyed per variant so the five lattice stones carry five distinct surface responses from ROCK_SURFACE_VARIANTS (rockSurfaceLibrary.js:17-25): tint, roughness, ao, normalScale. That per-variant split is deliberate, not waste — it prevents one texture reading as five painted copies (rockSurfaceLibrary.js:10-16). Note the runtime variant is hashId(entity.id)%5 (visualFactory.js:2642), so the ledger's variant0..4 are five buckets of the same builder, not fixed assets. Role is the matte absorber with zero emissive (153-157). No inclusions (293-297). LOD: no body swap; only detail hiding applies and stone has no details.
decision: No construction change recommended; geometry is shared with the ordinary rock pool and the per-variant material is intentional. Recommend needs follow-up: visual evidence for matte/mirror/prism separation is the acceptance path.
next: Needs a current gameplay-scale and close capture of the stone border beside diamond and metal (ceres prism gallery or swarm arena) plus measured draw cost.

observation: Captured as a live asteroid entity (typeId ast_common_rock, data.opticMaterial=stone) through vf.build -> buildAsteroid -> opticCellPresentation.js. Entity id 6 lands hashId(id)%5 = 0 — selects BOTH the astDisplacedGeometry displacement bucket and the cached optic:body:stone:v0 surface material (ROCK_SURFACE_VARIANTS[0]). matte absorber — shared displaced ast_common_rock geometry + per-variant optic:body:stone:vN material. opticFinal=true confirms the decoded rock-surface maps are bound. All 3 frames ok=true; the five variants differ only by surface response on shared geometry, as designed.
decision: Capture evidence produced for the ledger target; final visual acceptance belongs to the orchestrator.
